rec_texts: As to who has the right to begin on the argument of
the objection, the cases differ. See Bradstock vs.
Whatley,6 Beaven, 451; Attorney General vs. Gard-
ner,2 Collyer,564; Lovelt vs. Andrew,11 Jurist,835:
When the objection is not taken before the hearing,
the Court has a discretionary power to make a decree
without prejudice to the absent parties,

It may be here observed that the Court seldom exer-
cises this power, and more frequently adjourns cases to
have parties added, although the objection has been
taken neither by answer nor on the argument. It is
always safe therefore to amend the record as soon as any
defect for want of parties is apprehended.
